items.sum: Leg-by-leg report of the London to Brighton Relay (Southern Clubs), in which Belgrave finished third behind Thames Valley and Herne Hill, with individual times.
items.s: Road Relay Running Leg-by-leg report of the London to Brighton Relay (Southern Clubs), in which Belgrave finished third behind Thames Valley and Herne Hill, with individual times. LONDON TO BRIGHTON RELAY (SOUTHERN CLUBS) OCTOBER 13TH. The "Gods" again smiled on us and provided us with another fine day for the second of our bi-annual visits to that famed Regency resort,Brighton. The reporters in the Sunday newspaper organising these races,gave us no chance of winning (as always) which in itself automatically assured us of at least a place. The better-informed thought we might be second to T.V.H, but Herne Hill,now appearing near the front with alarming regularity, proved them wrong by a mere 16 secs.However,this is anticipating our story,so let us proceed. Len Bishop,in place of our regular first runner,P.Bagnall, who was injured,rose well above the form he had shown of late, giving us a reasonably good start finishing 6th behind Poly,H.H.H Aylesford, Hampstead,and St.Albans in that order. Eric Gebbett,more used to 15 and 20 miles than a mere 5,soon proved that he has a turn of speed,quickly passing St.Albans and Hampstead.Poly unfortunately lost their way at tha start of this leg,and dropped to 10th.At Wandsworth H.H.H led from Aylesford and Woodford with Eric not far away.An ominous cloud,in the form of Ken Norris of T.V.H was looming up,and not dismayed by their 10th position on the 1st. leg,he ripped through the field and headed the race before the take-over,as if the hounds of hell were at his heels. He established a lead of 89secs. and chopped 54secs.off the stage record.Eric was undeterred however,and ran steadily throughout to hand over 3rd.behind T.V.H and Woodford,having made up 3 places. Charlie Dabbs,on the long leg from Mitcham to Purley,had the misfortune to start only a few seconds ahead of Ken Caulder of Surrey, Sando, and Towl of H.H.H. Charlie wisely ran his own race,arriving in Purley in 6th. place,just over 2 minutes behind the leaders T.V.H Came George Davidson and hopes that some of the leeway would be made up as George had run so well in the recent road race. Although by no means disgracing himself,he could make no impression and was forced to give way to Thorpe of St.Albans.The experience should be invaluable to George in the future. Jumbo Masters,who we were glad to see out in the team again, set about the opposition through Redhill,passing St.Albans,now exhausted of their supply of good runners,and Surrey,handing over well within striking distance of all but T.V.H.Jumbo had put up the fastest time on hig leg. Ray Tooby,another of our experienced runners who had missed a few Brightons,took over on the flat 5mls.run to Lowfield Heath with three runners in sight.He ran steadily,but his effort lacked spirit,and we made no further headway.We were now 2½ mins down. On the longest leg of all,Jack Brown ran a "blinder",making up 2 places and 30secs on T.V.H.His time was surpassed only by St. Albans' O'Gorman,at that time well behind us.Jack gave Heywood of H.H.H a fright and was unlucky not to catch him before Handcross. The traffic here was exceptionally thick and a slight contretemps with a large car might well have proved serious to our runners. Pete Newall took over on the second longest leg from Hickstead, and although making good progress down Handcross Hill,later regretted this fast start,as many have before him.He quickly caught Ron Clarke, but experience soon prevailed,and Ron steadily pulled away.A game but very tired Newall handed his baton to Geoff Goode at "The Castle" 3mins behind T.V.H and 1¼mins behind H.H.H but still in 3rd position. Geoff was another newcomer to the Brighton trail,and after a good start seemed to be suffering badly on what is thought to be a fairly easy leg,but which is in fact a " snorter " as the writer, in company with other distinguished Club members can well vouch for. However,Geoff pulled himself together and moved well over the last mile in sight of the South Downs. At the foot of Dale Hill,Charlie Walker waited,as usual, wasting much energy asking all and sundry," what do you think?" Would Charlie pull one out of the bag and put us back in the running for 2nd place? By now the winners were almost a foregone conclusion. It was certainly Walker's day when, 97 secs.behind H.H.H., represented by promising J.Davis, he climbed Dale Hill like a champion, and with the aid of continuous encouragement from supporting occupants of cars, the most prominent being the President, he produced the fastest time of the day and took us to within 64 secs. of the "Hill". T.V.H. unfortunately, also had a good performer on this leg and only 6 secs. was pared from their lead, which mattered little as they were now over ½ mile ahead. Dave Baulch, whose running during the summer was a source of disappointment to many (including Mavis) set out to prove his fitness, and with a time of 17.40 on the last leg, a time beaten only by a few Belgravians, raised hopes of our finishing 2nd. Unfortunately the race could not be extended to Black Rock or we should certainly have pegged back those red and black hoops. As it was, a mere 100 yds. separated us from the 2nd team and Dave did the fastest of the day. We can be well satisfied with our effort. Experience has been given to newcomers to this event, which will help us next April, and now that S.L.H. have lost the great Gordon and we can improve on our team by the inclusion of Davies and Hallowell, it can be hoped that last year's 5th position in the National Relay can be bettered by at least 4 places. items.sum: Walking report on the Chippenham to Calne 6 miles, won by George Coleman, with Belgrave narrowly missing third team place, and results.
items.s: Walking Notes: Chippenham to Calne 6 Miles. Walking report on the Chippenham to Calne 6 miles, won by George Coleman, with Belgrave narrowly missing third team place, and results. Not quite the same star-studded field as in previous years tackled this tough course in lovely weather. We had eleven starters but were without Stan Vickers. Wally Emery put a Belgrave vest in front early on, but unfortunately split his heel and had to retire. Belgrave men, it seemed, were everywhere, and if all had been eligible to score we would have won the team event; as it was we missed third place by one point and were only eight points behind Metropolitan Walking Club, the winners. George Coleman added to his list of triumphs and missed the course record held by R. Hardy by only ten seconds. His opposition were disqualified early on and he won by 2m.39s. in 44m.19s. Next came Eric Hall followed by second claim member George Williams in 47m.38s. Ray Hall gained revenge on Ray Switzer, Norman Guilmant smiled his way through and was last seen selling old football jerseys to the timekeepers. Dennis Russell showed us that he will get his seven-mile badge very soon. It was pleasing to see Doug Woods again and we hope that this is the first of many appearances Doug. Ray Switzer got another crafty fourth handicap and Ray Hall crept in at the last with tenth place while Charlie Speechley was only just behind. This shows an improvement on last year so what about next year lads, lets have our share of the pork pies which go with the first team prize. Eric Hall. 1st. G. Coleman H.H. 44.19 27th. N. items.sum: Report of the St. Dunstans one hour walks at Parliament Hill, where Stan Vickers set a meeting record and Belgrave won the team race.
items.s: St. Dunstans One Hour Walks Report of the St. Dunstans one hour walks at Parliament Hill, where Stan Vickers set a meeting record and Belgrave won the team race. Parliament Hill 22nd. Sept. Quite a good muster of 26 members took part in the various sections. Highlight of "D" section was John Knifton's fine effort in finishing second with a distance of 6 mls. 795 yds. Ben, his father, competing on the same afternoon, must have been pleased with his 17 year-old son's performance. George Webb gained his 6 mile badge, whilst Bob Readman only just missed his 7 mile. Surely Bob has earned the name "Evergreen"- a grand effort. Ray Switzer, ably backed up by Ray Hall, Dave Stevens and Eric Froude gained his 7 mile badge in this section. Peak of this meeting, is the "A" section, and we saw a grand performance by our lads. Stan Vickers led from the start, followed by George Coleman and at the mile they were 6 m.56s. and 7 m. 3s. respectively. Although Coleman got within 60 yds. of Stan, he could get no nearer and Stan went on to a meeting record of 8 mls. 120 yds. With fine efforts from Eric Hall, Ted Smith, George Checkley and Bob Newson, the latter practically killing himself to take Stan over the last couple of laps, we won the team race from Woodford Green. Well done all concerned - a fine show. J. Goswell. Walking report of the match against M.P.A.A. at Wimbledon, won by Belgrave 392 points to 337 with George Checkley first, plus handicap and positions. This event always marks the opening of our winter fixtures and although some of our lads had travelled to Chippenham for the open event, held on the same day, a field of 38 faced the starter. After some early dashes to the front, a group, including Checkley and Newson, settled down in the lead. George Checkley walked really well to win in 40m.12s. with Bob Newson second, Syd James (whom we are pleased to see out again) third and Eric Froude, still improving, fourth. With quite a number of our lads representing M.P.A.A. we expected a close result, and scoring 18 a side we won by 392 points to 337. The handicap was won by our youngest member John Knifton, so "look out the handicapper". George Webb was second and Bert Stevenson third. As this was the first time any of these chaps had won a pot everyone was well pleased. Fred Freeman won the prize for the first M.P.A.A. man home. Handicap. There is always a small field for this championship owing to call up etc., but this year we had a good little team competing. Ray Middleton, home from Ireland, walked well to finish 6th in 41m.21s., Dave Stevens (individual) was 7th, Nick Milsum 9th and Terry Clark, who walked a blinder on the last lap, was 12th and Trevor Luck 13th. Trowbridge A.C., with 1st and 2nd won the team event with 13 points although their third man was 20th. Belgrave were 2nd with 17 points thanks to Terry Clark's effort, as we tied with Metropolitan W.C. and placing depended upon the third man. Our future looks bright with these rapidly improving lads. items.label: No. 129
items.sum: Report of the pre-Olympic 10 miles walk trial at Brighton, showing Stan Vickers recovered from injury and Eric Hall walking well before the Melbourne Olympics.
items.s: Pre-Olympic Walk 10 Miles - Brighton 3rd.Nov. Report of the pre-Olympic 10 miles walk trial at Brighton, showing Stan Vickers recovered from injury and Eric Hall walking well before the Melbourne Olympics. Although this race was not taken too seriously,everybody was anxious to see how Stan Vickers had recovered from his leg trouble. In the previous weeks,rumours had flown thick and fast concerning him.After watching Stan and Eric Hall in this trial,we feel sure they will be a credit to their Country and Club,at Melbourne. Stan kept with Hardy and Coleman in the lead until 8-8½ mls but then dropped 5 yards or so.He recovered again and was with the leaders when they went off course after being misdirected,and lost at least ½ ml.After retracing their steps,they decided to walk back together to the stadium. K.Matthews,who had been some 500yards behind when the leaders went off course,was only a few yards behind at the stadium,and whilst lapping the track,decided to pass the three men,which really meant nothing;they were content to stroll in chatting together. Their time 77.16 for over 10½mls indicates the early speed of the race.Eric Hall had walked a very well controlled effort and gradually moved through the field to finish as the 1st Kilos man home in 79.47 for 10mls. We can be justly proud of Stan and Eric,who fully justified their selection.Good luck to them both! J. Goswell. items.label: No. 129
items.sum: Note that member John Bromley, a former steeplechaser, won the 17-mile Singapore to Jahore walking race for the second year.
items.s: John Bromley wins big walk. Note that member John Bromley, a former steeplechaser, won the 17-mile Singapore to Jahore walking race for the second year. We are indebted to a member of Thames Valley Harriers for the report of a Walking Race from Singapore to Jahore,a distance of just over 17 miles,which was won by none other than John Bromley former steeplechaser and Brighton Relay runner in the very good time of 2hrs.56mins. This race,which was promoted by the Singapore Free Press,was held on a Sunday morning,when no less than 650 competitors lined up for the start at 6am. According to press cuttings,John won this race last year,but has apparently kept his achievement up his sleeve as this appears to be the first intimation that he has turned to road walking.We do like to hear of the activities of our members who are overseas and hope that any others who are carrying on the good work will let us know about it. Of the 650 starters,430 finished the course,and John received once again the handsome trophy presented for annual competition by Messrs Bata,the shoe people,and the prize of a cinecamera presented by Twentieth Century Fox Films Ltd. Well done John. Bill True is making note of the result in case you continue walking on your return to this country. S.C.R. items.sum: Note from the new Youth and Junior Section secretary on training packs at Wimbledon, with results of a junior 3 mile road race and a 4 lap road relay at Battersea Park.
items.s: For the Attention of all Juniors and Youths Note from the new Youth and Junior Section secretary on training packs at Wimbledon, with results of a junior 3 mile road race and a 4 lap road relay at Battersea Park. This article is primarily for the benefit of the Youth and Junior Section of our club, of which you, the members, have nominated me as Secretary. There are a few points I would like to make which I feel some of you would like to know. ONE. is that I am always ready to listen to any suggestion as regards the functions of our sections. TWO. I am endeavouring to form one, or more training packs during the Winter months; at the moment, we are training from Wimbledon on Tuesday and Thursday nights at 7-0 pm. and Saturday afternoons. I am grading the packs to enable runners of varying ability to enjoy these runs and also to develop each individual without his being run off his legs. This is most important as every Champion will tell you pack running is the foundation of Team running by which we can endeavour to win the Major Events during the Cross Country Season. There are two results which apply to our Section:- 3 Mile Road Race at Wimbledon 29.9.56 K. Miller is a new member and shows every promise. 4 Lap Road Relay at Battersea Park 21.10.56. This race was organised by M. Pyer. and was arranged to give our younger members a chance to show what they could do. Their ages ranged from 12½ to 15½ years. One of our members, E. Penny, recorded second fastest time over the course, which is approximately 1¾ miles. His time was 8 mins. 49secs. which is very good running, but a Mitcham lad did even better- his time being 8 mins. 42 secs. A. W. Penny. (Secretary) Junior Section. 1. A.W.Black - 15.41. 2. K. items.sum: Teasing notes about cross-country runners neglecting club nights at Belgrave Hall, not wearing Belgrave vests and skipping an away road relay.
items.s: Stirrings Teasing notes about cross-country runners neglecting club nights at Belgrave Hall, not wearing Belgrave vests and skipping an away road relay. It is a pity that some Cross-Country Runners (not Night-School Students) who manage the journey to run at Wimbledon some evenings, have apparently forgotten the whereabouts of Belgrave Hall on Club Nights. Members may be assured that if they bring their shampoo on Tuesday or Thursday we can arrange for the extractor fan to be dismantled and converted into a hair dryer. An assurance has been received that in the later cross-country events, runners at present so allergic to their Belgrave vests when representing their Club will wear them. Do they mean when they should be in their County vests? It is heartbreaking to learn that the official reason for not supporting an away road relay where free overnight accommodation had been promised was given as the reluctance of runners to miss their Sunday morning training run!!! Wimbledon Belgrave Hall

items.label: No. 130
items.sum: Editorial asking members to send in regular reports, explaining a plan to post the magazine with the fixture cards, and urging full Belgrave support in all matches for the 1957 season.
items.s: EDITORIAL Editorial asking members to send in regular reports, explaining a plan to post the magazine with the fixture cards, and urging full Belgrave support in all matches for the 1957 season. Dear Fellow Members, Once upon a time, we used to read this magazine, and we often wondered why it was that the editors were repeatedly asking the officials of each branch of the Club, to send in REGULAR reports of its activities, together with any other items of interest. Now we know! We are not magicians, and cannot be expected to prepare the magazine in the few days immediately before it is due to be printed. To lighten our task therefore, we must ask that reports be sent to us weekly, BY ANYONE, be he spectator, competitor or official. In fact, the wider the field of contribution, the greater the interest of the magazine. What could be more simple than scribbling a report on the way home in the train? Furthermore, in the interests of economy, it is hoped to combine the despatch of the Belgravian with that of the fixture cards, thereby saving approximately £10 per annum. This cannot be achieved unless the magazine can be completed each quarter and sent for printing on time. So let's be hearing from all you budding reporters. We would like to thank those anonymous contributors who have sent us articles for this edition. No doubt they will appreciate that where we receive more than one report on the same event, the contents, as near as possible, are combined, and any loss of style will be understood. By the time this edition is distributed, the track season will be with us, and the programme of long distance road races will have commenced. We want to see full Belgrave support in all the major events, on the Track, in Field Events, and on the Road. Whilst agreeing that athletics is a sport to be enjoyed, win or lose, we feel that the time has come for us to endeavour to assert ourselves as the premier club in the South, and to do this by putting our full strength into all matches. We have an abundance of talent in our ranks, at all ages. Messrs. Carter, Footer, Penny, Herbert, Green, Scrimshaw, Lucas and Stimpson were no more endowed than some of our present men; they merely exploited their gifts more by plenty of hard training and by turning out regularly in all Club matches. Everyone must start at the bottom, and none is so good that he can afford to ignore minor events. The presence of a "Star" in a race is a challenge to the lesser lights to topple him from his pedestal, and he learns that only hard work will keep him there. The unknown having tasted victory will be eagerly looking around for his next "head". Keen competition within the Club for team places is the key to success, but it must be made certain that there are sufficient "B" team matches to enable second string men to gain that experience necessary for promotion to the "A" team. We hope to be reporting the successful commencement of the 1957 season in our next issue. Your coaches can only guide you, you must do the work. Your success will be their well-deserved reward. So go to it and good luck! Your Editors. items.s: SOUTH OF THAMES JUNIOR. 10th. NOV. Report of a poor Belgrave turnout at the South of Thames Junior cross-country race at Brighton, with Charlie Dabbs 8th and the A, B and D team placings. SOUTH OF THAMES JUNIOR. 10th. NOV. Is the Brighton seaside air not encouraging enough itself or does the thought of a journey frighten many Belgravians? Whatever it was, there was a poor turnout for this event - less in fact, than half those entered. I would add that one of our newer members' worked until midday and then journeyed down by train to compete. The race itself was disappointing from the point of view of Club supporters, who were also few in number. Charlie Dabbs gave of his best again and finished 8th., but I feel much credit should go to J. Dooley, who although entered in the "D" team, finished 54th. to be the third Belgrave man home. As for the other competing members, I am sure they would all admit to having had better runs than this. Once again Arthur Whitehead must be thanked for supplying a very welcome cup of tea to all our runners at the finish. Placings and team positions:- 7th.Belgrave "A" ( 8 C. Dabbs, 50 G. items.s: CITY OF ROCHESTER 5 mile ROAD RACE 17th NOV. 1956 Report of Jack Brown winning the City of Rochester 5 mile road race from Salvat of Finchley, with Ray Tooby 12th and Len Bishop 46th. CITY OF ROCHESTER 5 mile ROAD RACE 17th NOV. 1956 The usual cold, misty weather greeted the starters for this year's race, but soon warming to his task, Jack Brown set about the opposition in no uncertain manner and was soon in the leading bunch with Salvat of Finchley and Cameron of T.V.H. Jack and Salvat ran neck and neck until approximately 500yds from the finish, when Jack's fine burst of speed proved too much for his opponent. The winning time was only 8sec. outside George Knight's course record. Ray Tooby, continuing his welcome return to form, ran very well to finish 12th, only three seconds behind Haslam (T.V.H.). Len Bishop who arrived only just in time for the start, finished 46th. It was a pity we did not have more support for this event, as no doubt we could have been placed in the team race. 1st J.W. "BLACKSTAFFE" SHIELD RACE 8th DEC. 1956 The annual 7miles C.C. Championship took place on a wet and misty afternoon over a slightly longer course than the one used last year. Jack Brown ran very impressively to win by a full minute from Charlie Walker with Ray Tooby half a minute further back in third place. Steve Charlton, showing much improved form, deservedly won the handicap. Second place in the handicap went to Clive Shippen who finished 5th in the actual race - a very good performance. It is very unusual for the scratch man to be placed in a sealed handicap, but in securing third place, Jack Brown achieved this feat. Eric Herbert, making one of his rare appearances, proved that he is still running quite well by finishing ninth. Also taking part was Jack Braughton who has now become a first claim member. items.sum: Report of Belgrave winning the Mitcham 15 team award, with Jack Brown beating O'Gorman and cutting 41 seconds off Jim Peters' course record; the text places Len Bishop 15th but the result and a later sentence give 14th.
items.s: THE MITCHAM"15" JAN. 12th. Report of Belgrave winning the Mitcham 15 team award, with Jack Brown beating O'Gorman and cutting 41 seconds off Jim Peters' course record; the text places Len Bishop 15th but the result and a later sentence give 14th. THE MITCHAM"15" JAN. 12th. Our road runners notched a further great victory when providing the individual winner of this very popular event and carrying off the team award. Continuing along his road of success Jack Brown sliced off 41 seconds from Jim Peters course record, a most meritorious performance. The race seemed to resolve itself quite rapidly into two fierce battles, between O'Gorman, Brown, Keily, Hicks, Lambert and Haslam on the one hand and a close bunch of a dozen, including our own trio, Colin Collis, Eric Gebbett and Len Bishop on the other. Jack and O'Gorman, however, had what appeared to be a burning desire to be all alone and with a big effort between 5 and 9 miles (at which point the time was 44m 30s!) they had established a lead of 20 seconds. Any hopes of individual honours cherished by the following group had by now completely vanished. The further these two went, the diminutive O'Gorman and the taller Jack, his hair bouncing with each stride, the greater the gap became, and Keily, who had moved up to third, was soon almost out of sight. Colin, Eric and Len were firmly dug in at 8th, 9th and 15th respectively and Jim Heathfield, confounding everyone, looked very comfortable in 28th place. The wise head of Collis had obviously intervened in Jim's training. Back to the leaders, where, with 400 yds. to go, Jack produced an amazing turn of speed which completely overwhelmed O'Gorman, with the incredible result that Jack ran out the winner by 14 seconds! It is indeed food for thought when one realises that these two had run throughout at approximately 4m.58s. per mile; how about the marathon Jack? With Eric and Colin finishing in good style 8th and 9th, no doubts were felt about the team result. A word of consolation to Len Bishop for finishing 14th in a fast time, yet being denied a team prize. However, let this be a reminder that road-running honours are going to be difficult to come by this season. It was good to see our London to Brighton men, Alan Bishop, MacDonald and Wortley sharpening up early in the season, it is hoped they will soon be starting their long preparation. A special word of praise to Jim Heathfield, whose time of 89m.28s. would open the eyes of many considered road runners. If the Mitcham "15" is any criterion, then the Belgrave vest will be well to the fore in all the leading road events during 1957. items.s: CLUB 10 MILES CROSS-COUNTRY CHAMPIONSHIP 26th JAN. 1957 Report and result of the club 10 miles cross-country championship, won by Jack Brown for the eighth successive Macher Shield, with Paget winning the handicap. CLUB 10 MILES CROSS-COUNTRY CHAMPIONSHIP 26th JAN. 1957 Although the course was below the stipulated distance (approximately 9¾ miles), the times were nevertheless very fast. In addition the terrain was rather muddy in places and light rain was falling during most of the race. The field was off to a fast start but it was not until just after the brook that Jack Brown managed to drop Charlie Walker. Coming up to four miles Brown had a lead of one hundred yards on Walker, with Dave Baulch a similar distance adrift, followed by Eric Gebbett and Ray Tooby a little way behind. At eight miles Brown was 1 min. 20 sec. to the good, with Walker 20 sec. in front of Baulch, and Tooby, having pulled away from Gebbett, now running fourth. Over the last couple of miles there were no positional changes amongst the leaders, but the distance between them lengthened, and at the finish Brown came home an easy winner in the excellent time of 50m.27s. Jack must be congratulated on winning the "Macher Shield" for the eighth time in succession, but we must also extend our congratulations to Charlie Walker—for indeed it is no disgrace to be runner-up to Jack—and Dave Baulch for a really splendid performance. Carnival Dance 26th Jan. 1957 Once again the Social Section of the Club did a fine job, and a good time was had by all. Stan Vickers and Ray Hall again acted as Phillip Harbens in the Sausage and Mash Supper Comedy, this time ably assisted by Mrs. Goswell and Mrs. Knifton, who took the part of Mrs. Beatons. Dancing went very well with all the old-timers lowering their dignity to do rock n' roll; it was a treat to watch. The various games and activities (mainly organised by Bill Lucas) proved very pleasant interludes, as well as a source of great enjoyment both to those taking part and to those watching. The A.T.C. Skiffle Group provided some very lively interval music - thanks boys. It only remains for me to ask "When's the next dance?" ANNUAL HALF-HOUR PAARLAUF. CHRISTMAS This event would have had much more support had there not been a friendly fixture with Herne Hill on the same day. When it is considered how much work Arthur Whitehead puts in to this race he must find it very discouraging to have his efforts (unwittingly it is hoped) sabotaged in this manner. The race itself, run in very pleasant weather, resolved into a dual between a Belgrave pair, Charlie Walker and C. Henn, and two Hercules runners, who together with four others had been invited to compete. When the signal, indicating three minutes to go, was given, Charlie and D. Cobb of Hercules were running together in the lead. It is a very difficult business to try to estimate just how much time is left but Charlie managed it to a nicety and putting in his effort with about ten seconds to go, drew away to win by several yards. items.s: MATCH V. WESTMINSTER BANK AT EPSOM 28th Dec. Report of a Belgrave team winning an eight-mile cross-country match against Westminster Bank at Epsom by one point, with Flanagan first. MATCH V. WESTMINSTER BANK AT EPSOM 28th Dec. As there was an"A" team match at Wimbledon on the same day we were fortunate in mustering nine runners at Epsom for this pleasant little fixture. The course of eight miles was genuine cross-country, consisting of hills, mud and plough, with a short stretch of road. Flanagan ran very well to finish first, beating Gilham of the Bank by 15 sec. They were followed by three Bank runners but as the next six were all Belgravians, the balance was tipped slightly in our favour and we won by one point - a very fair result. Afterwards we were entertained to tea, for which we were very grateful, and a somewhat strenuous afternoon was brought to a fitting conclusion. Our hosts expressed the wish that we might visit them again next year - fixture committee please take note ! items.s: SOUTH OF THE THAMES SENIOR Report of the South of the Thames senior cross-country race at Maidenhead, where the Belgrave team finished only 15th, complaining that no individual results were sent in. SOUTH OF THE THAMES SENIOR Held at Maidenhead on Feb. 2nd over an extremely heavy course this race proved a big disappointment for the Club when our team could finish only 15th. We do not agree with the view held in some parts of the Club, that reports of races in which the Club is unsuccessful should be withheld from this magazine. This attitude, which we feel is quite wrong, probably explains the almost complete lack of news from the Cross-Country Section. We cannot therefore give any details of individual performances in this race as they are not in our possession. We can only hope that someone will do something to remedy this unsatisfactory state of affairs and see to it that we are regularly supplied with results, be they favourable or otherwise. South of the Thames Senior Maidenhead

items.s: NEW YEAR CELEBRATIONS DEC.29th. Account of the Social Committee's New Year celebrations, with a bangers-and-mash supper, games, a skiffle band and thanks to Bill Lucas as M.C. and Tom Carter. NEW YEAR CELEBRATIONS DEC.29th. It seems an understatement to say the evening was a resounding success, in the light of the gaiety, fun, entertainment and the whole gamut of carefreeness devised by our Social Committee. Bangers, grilled to a turn, potatoes, bashed and pounded to insensibility by a team of master cooks, headed by such International figures as Messieurs Vickers, Hall and Goswell with a posse of Presidents to act as scullions. The resulting "Chef-d'oeuvre", supported by lashings of tea, rolls and butter, etc., was treated with suspicion until the full delicacy of the masterly preparation was appreciated with cries more. This was a prelude to a programme of carnival festivities which for gaiety, fun and whole-hearted co-operation from all, led to an ever-to-be-remembered evening. Nothing appeared forgotten or left to chance. That difficult warming up period was successfully negotiated by a series of games, chief of which was sniffing at mysterious looking bags. The consequent fun soon broke the ice. A "Skiffle Band" performance introduced by Eric Penny thoroughly livened up the interval and the numerous encores were sufficient proof of appreciation. Thank you Eric and your colleagues for their grand show. It is unnecessary to dwell on the lovely and charming ladies present, they were indeed all beautiful, sufficient to thank them for their presence and co-operation; our reward is to see them so thoroughly enjoying themselves. Finally a word of appreciation to our Social Committee for a wonderful evening, particularly to Bill Lucas for his grand job as M.C. to which we were all indebted, and to Tom Carter for all his work so enthusiastically carried out. items.sum: Report of the Southern Counties cross-country championships at Epsom, where the Belgrave senior team finished 3rd behind South London and Thames Valley, led by Jack Brown, with junior and youths race notes and positions.
items.s: SOUTHERN COUNTIES C.C. CHAMPS. EPSOM. FEB.16th. Report of the Southern Counties cross-country championships at Epsom, where the Belgrave senior team finished 3rd behind South London and Thames Valley, led by Jack Brown, with junior and youths race notes and positions. SOUTHERN COUNTIES C.C. CHAMPS. EPSOM. FEB.16th. Senior race. We are back amongst the top Southern clubs again as a result of the fine performance of our team in finishing 3rd. behind South London and Thames Valley. Our six scoring men, led by Jack Brown, were all well placed throughout, and whilst commendably they held those placings, one did not see the spectacle of the claret and gold vests moving up through the field in last desperate attempts to whittle away those points. However, let nothing detract from their performance, it was a welcome and heartening sight, and it should not be overlooked that the course was one mile short. A fast start saw a keen struggle for the lead with our second claim member, Bill Bird of Ranelagh actually leading during the early stages. Ken Norris and Peter Driver soon asserted themselves however, and pulled away from Ibbotson and Firth. Jack Brown was well placed, closely followed by Pete Newell, making one of his rare appearances and proving that potentially he is a first class cross-country runner. Then came Chas. Walker, Pete Bagnall, Dave Baulch and Eric Gebbett, all running strongly and all four within reach of one another but unable apparently to join forces, a fact which probably cost us second team place. Although still very husky from a heavy cold, Shippen was about the 100 mark with Len Bishop, Eddie Short and Jim Heathfield further back. And so it was, our lads hung on grimly to their early gains and ran out a good third with Jack Brown, a little disappointed perhaps, our first man home. The Bels were ably backed up by the moral and vocal support of many members, and it was good to see Tom Carter, a most decididly active President, whipping 'em up along the line. Many of us know from past experience, especially as juniors, what encouragement is derived from the attendance of Club officials of whatever capacity, at events of this nature. This was brought to mind even more by the presence of Ernie Duffett, whom we were glad to see looking fit and well. Arthur Penny seems to have earned the respect and loyalty of those juniors under his care and it is to be hoped that his efforts will be rewarded next year by some real team running again in those events in which we were once so prominent. Latent talent will not pass Arthur's eye unnoticed. Our sages tell us that we always perform better in the National than in the Southern, so let us look to even better news after the Parliament Hill battlefield on March 9th. Positions :- 10, J.W. items.s: WALKING NOTES. Walking notes congratulating the club's Olympic walkers, welcoming new juniors, and appealing for support for the track season and the Brighton walk. WALKING NOTES. These are, of necessity, brief, but tell of the continued progress of the Club. To others I have left the Olympics, but I am sure I echo the sentiments of all when I say, "Well done Eric and Stan, you were a credit in every way to the Club". With these two, ably backed up, we have great hopes of winning the National 10 again; Sheffield eight years running is too much! Tuesday evenings throughout the Winter have seen good turn-outs at the hall. As a result we lead the Southern clubs in the Winter "Opens" again. We have a fine crowd of up and coming Juniors and welcome Bryan Cormick, George Barratt, M. Small and John Gilbert. May they look back with pride on the day they became "Bels". Coach Don Brown is always pleased to help you, and we start our track season soon. We want a good school at Battersea on Tues. and Thurs.; it is essential to all short distance men, whom we look to, to regain our Inter-Club Track Title this year, whilst we hope the long distance men also retain our hard won titles. I hope to issue dates of fixtures we are supporting this year, along with the R.W.A. 20 and Kilos and the Brighton. We look forward to a grand Summer and to A.A.A. titles for Stan and ....? - who knows? Rally round supporters, your vocal efforts are needed to drive the "Bels" along. Unless we get more support we may have to discontinue the hire of a coach for the Brighton; a nearly empty coach on the journey down is such an expense - the competitors could more cheaply return by train. Let me know early please so that I can see whether a coach is warranted. Training with a happy crowd is great fun. Experiences gained are many. Stan Vickers, back from Melbourne, revealed his prowess in cooking "Bangers". Come along, join in the good fellowship that is to be had. Reap the benefits of FITNESS. In closing, my thanks to all who have helped me in various ways during a busy season. By their ever-ready help and co-operation they enabled the Club to stage another successful Open Walk and the S.R.W.A. Garnet Cup Championship. Thank you, one and all, Yours, Jack Goswell. CLUB 10 MILES CHAMPIONSHIP (MURPHY SHIELD) Chiefly due to a clash with the Stock Exchange 7 miles championships, only 29 walkers started, and we were without Stan Vickers, Ray Hall and Dave Stevens. Eric Hall retained his title, winning by 34 sec. from 2nd claim member George Williams who had travelled up from Worcester (that's enthusiasm). In the champioship Dave McMullen was 2nd and Syd James 3rd. Dave just pipped Williams for the handicap with Bob Readman a popular 3rd. What a pity Bob's new job prevents regular attendance, our youngsters could benefit from him. A match versus Met. Police was held in conjunction with the race which we won by scoring 90 pts. to 192. items.s: RESULTS OF COUNTY 10 MILES CHAMPIONSHIPS 23RD FEBRUARY, 1957 Reports and results of the Surrey, Kent and Middlesex 10 miles walking championships, with Eric Hall winning Surrey, Stan Vickers Kent, and Belgrave walkers placing second for Cadogan A.C. in Middlesex; the Surrey text gives Switzer 9th and Coleman 10th while the table gives 10th and 11th. RESULTS OF COUNTY 10 MILES CHAMPIONSHIPS 23RD FEBRUARY, 1957 SURREY AT MITCHAM We started two teams, and 44 walkers faced the started in driving rain. Eric Hall took the lead, closely followed by George Williams. Eric broke away after half-a-mile and thereafter was in no danger of defeat. 63 sec. up at the half distance, he won by 2 min.15sec. from George, who had walked well and always held second place from Dave McMullen who suffered from cramp at 7 miles, but held 3rd place, finishing almost 2 min. ahead of the fourth man. We scored 1,2,3, with Ray Switzer 9th and Joe Coleman 10th. Ray Hall, walking as an individual gained County colours by finishing 6th. Jim Edwards, in his first County 10, performed well. Our "B" team was completed by Joe Wilson, George Webb and Dan Logan, who suffered from the cold. What a distance man Webb would make with regular training! He has obvious potential. Summing up - a grand repeat performance by Eric and a first class team. 43 finished KENT AT BEXLEY Stan Vickers retained his title, winning by the incredible margin of 7m.32s. in 78m.14s. Another new course record (that's three on the trot). Well done Stan! MIDDLESEX AT EASTCOTE Driving rain for a couple of hours or so before the start of this race threatened almost impossible conditions, but fortunately it eased as the competitors started on the hilly course. We had eight walkers competing for Cadogan A.C. and although our chances of a win were slender, we were not without hope. Metropolitan W.C. soon put paid to these by a splendid exhibition of team walking, eventually winning with the absolute mimimum score of 10pts., finishing the first four home. Ted Smith was our great hope for the individual title and at two miles had a lead of afew yards over the field. From the three mile point however, he must have become very tired at the sight of Met vests for he found himself walking with six or seven of their men from then on. Eventually Ted finished sixth, a creditable performance. George Checkley walked strongly in the second half of the race, gaining several places and finishing just in front of Bob Newson who walked evenly throughout. Our fourth man, Hugh McGreechan lost several places in the last two miles but our margin over the third club, Polytechnic H., was always an appreciable one. Of our others, Cyril Yescombe and Harry Shields had their usual social outing, and George Place and Syd Spencer seemed to enjoy their trip round this corner of Middlesex which still has fields and trees to show something remaining of a rural atmosphere. items.s: THE R.W.A. "GARNET CUP" CHAMPIONSHIP Report and result of the R.W.A. Garnet Cup 10 miles walk staged by Belgrave at Belgrave Hall, won by C. Williams of Ilford, with Belgrave 4th team and Ray Middleton their best man in 14th. THE R.W.A. "GARNET CUP" CHAMPIONSHIP At Belgrave Hall 2nd Feb. 1957 Local arrangements for this Southern 10 miles event (which is a "limited" Championship in that many barring clauses operate) were entrusted to us by the Race Walking Association; and we are confident that this trust was not misplaced. Our excellent accommodation at Belgrave Hall is indeed a great foundation to build upon, and with Jack Goswell and Arthur Whitehead working like beavers to ensure faultless arrangements for the planning and conduct of the race, and with Syd Roberts in charge of the scoring and recording details, we had all the ingredients for the perfect promotion. All that was needed in addition was reasonable weather and a good field - and these, too, were forthcoming. Stan Horton, Chairman of the R.W.A. Southern Area, started the field of 114 walkers, and C. Williams of Ilford A.C., the favourite, was soon in the lead and retained this to finish a very worthy winner from A.G. Thomson of Met. W.C. with M. Tadd of Brighton A.C. third. As our winning team of last year was no longer eligible and as many of our other walkers have previously shed their "Junior" status, we realised that our team prospects could not be considered of the brightest; but that they would give of their utmost we were sure, and we could not ask for more than that. The team race was keenly fought out and at one time was very open, but Met. W.C. gradually strengthened their hold to eventually finish easy winners. Woodford Green took second medals, and Brighton A.C., by two points, deprived us of third place. We had expected Trevor Luck to take a forward position in this year's race but he unfortunately broke a wrist a fortnight earlier, thus belying his name, and must wait another year. True he started but it was a forlorn hope with arm in plaster from wrist to elbow and training lost; he did well and revealed great pluck in finishing the race. Our three, Ray Middleton, Nick Milsum and Ray Switzer pursued a steady course together for the first half of the race and then began their advance through the field, with Middleton proving himself our best man on the day, finishing in 14th position. Our team was completed by Cyril Yescombe, and thereafter the Belgrave vests followed in at intervals until we had finished twelve men of the 107 completing the course. When next year's event comes round we are sure that many of our walkers will be showing that they have made progress; and one of our boys who should assuredly make the grade is John Keown. In conclusion, a pat on the back to our team and the assurance that we shall be among the placings again next year; and our renewed sincere thanks to all who helped with the event, with particular reference to the herculean labours of Jack and Arthur. items.sum: Eric Hall's account of the 1956 Melbourne Olympic Games, including the athletics highlights and the walks in which he and Stan Vickers competed.
items.s: THE OLYMPIC GAMES Eric Hall's account of the 1956 Melbourne Olympic Games, including the athletics highlights and the walks in which he and Stan Vickers competed. THE OLYMPIC GAMES By Eric Hall Our quarters were situated in the Olympic Village, Heidelburg, 10 miles from the Stadium and we reached them at 7a.m. on 12th Nov.1956 after a five day flight from London. The accommodation was pretty good except when it rained - as it did early in our stay - then everything was thick mud. Also excellent was the food, with great variety as well as quantity: indeed if one tackled every meal one couldn't do any training. The Opening Ceremony on Nov. 22nd will always be remembered as the big moment of the Games. We were driven the 10 miles to the stadium in coaches and the streets were lined with cheering crowds. The actual march of ¼ mile into the stadium was used by the crowd for some good-humoured bantering such as:- "Where's the Ashes?" "What about Jim Laker" We managed, however, to hold our own. At last the Games were open and we were greeted with our first spell of warm weather - 84degrees. Soon the athletes were holding the attention of over 100,000 spectators every day and on the Friday the first finals were decided. You know the results by now so I will not dwell on the details, but certain things, however, stick in one's memory at every athletic meeting. First of all, the machine-like running of Kuts - 400m steady, 70 to 100m fast - "steady" being 68s. in the 10,000m and faster still in the 5,000! Then the ease with which Bob Morrow completed the first double sprint victory since Jesse Owens's in 1936. Greg Bell long-jumping 25ft odd with a damaged leg-muscle which finally "went" on his last jump and Derek Johnson so nearly beating Tom Courtney in the 800m. One of the highlights of the Games was the high-jump duel between Dumas of the U.S.A. and unknown Porter of Australia - Dumas who found it too much trouble to convert metres to feet and Porter who peered at the bar before jumping. Bob Richards needed three attempts to qualify in the pole vault and Oerter, who had not seen a discus a year ago, won the Gold Medal, while our own Mark Pharaoh missed third place by five inches. In the javelin, Danielsen never really got loosened up until his last throw when he threw it almost out of the arena to record over 280ft. We had our sad moments also, the last Saturday proving the worst day, with our comparative failure in the 1500m - I do not mean failure in the extreme sense of the word, as a 4m.2s. mile is no flop! At that time I was out on the marathon course and saw Ron Clark and Fred Norris run themselves to a standstill and finally retire, to leave Harry Hicks gamely battling on to the finish, although being attacked with cramp on the track. However, our three relay teams kept the flag flying. The girls track events were shared amongst the Australians with our girls making the 100 & 200 metres finals, while the field events were dominated by the Russians. Perhaps the greatest moment of the Games, for me, was to see two of our men leading an Olympic field - and one of them a Belgravian. I mean of course, the 20km. walk in which Stan Vickers put up such a remarkable performance in holding off the Russians for so long and then giving chase in faultless style. Indeed, by his style, Stan earned for himself the title of "The Walker". I must not overlook the fact that we won a Gold Medal - all praise to Chris Brasher -"the hack who finally became a Champion". So much has been said and written about this event that I do not intend to say anything except that the two steeple-chasers, Rozsnyoi and Larsen, were great sportsmen. The 50km. walk brought us a spot of bother when Don Thompson, who was in fifth position at the time, collapsed from the heat with only 3kms. to go. He was taken to hospital but fortunately made a very quick recovery and now shows no ill effects. The feeding arrangements for this race and for the Marathon were good as was the policing of the courses. The judging in the 20km. walk left much to be desired and Stan should have had at least a bronze medal. However, we should be thankful for the fact that there were no international incidents. Stan was selected for the British Empire versus U.S.A. meeting but owing to the chaos it is not certain where he finished. He apparently had a good time in Sydney and it should be noted that the aforementioned city is now back to normal! We flew home via the United States, so making a round-the-world tour of 27,000 miles, a month's holiday and an unforgetable experience. As Stan says, "roll on 1960". Eric Hall P.S. We would both like to thank all those Club members who gave us their best wishes before we left. We would add that even if we didn't win we at least took part and had a very good try. E.W.H.& S.F.V. items.s: COACHING The Coaching Hon. Secretary lists the club's coaches for the coming season and invites offers of help and attendance at coaching courses. COACHING Our coaches these days may not be numerous but we will do all we can to assist anyone who will take the trouble to seek our advice. Frank Simmons will as usual be looking after the sprinters and relay-teams and putting in a tremendous amount of hard work. Stan Davies, Charlie Smart, Arthur Penny and George Isaac can give you assistance in the middle and long distances. Micky Pyer will be continuing his good work with the boys and youths and all our younger members should get to know him. I, myself, can, I hope, help all budding Field Events men and will seek to improve the better performers. Having mentioned that our Coaches are none too numerous, I would welcome any offers of assistance from people who think they are past their best and would like to help the younger members. A number of Coaching Courses are run throughout the season which, if attended, will give anyone a good insight into modern methods of training and technique. Some of these courses are for active athletes too and will benefit anyone who attends and more particularly if he takes his coach along with him. I shall have details of these from time to time and will be only too glad to pass them on to those interested. T.C. Jones, Coaching Hon. items.s: FIELD EVENTS GOSSIP Field events notes by T.C. Jones urging members to train and enter championships, aiming to retain the Sward Trophy at Chiswick, and reviewing the club's throwers and jumpers. FIELD EVENTS GOSSIP The Field Events Notes in the last issue were, I'm afraid, rather scanty owing to pressure of space. The Summer Season is fast approaching and I hope all Seniors, Juniors and Youths will be getting down to training in earnest for the coming fixtures. Your Captain, Mal Ash, Vice Captain Dave Ansell and myself want your full support so that we can turn out strong teams. What we want to see more than anything else is the name of Belgrave well represented in County, District and A.A.A. Championships. You may not be good enough to win or get a place but there are standard certificates or medals to be won. The entries of our Youths and Juniors are particularly needed in these events. I will be able to supply all information as to dates and venues of these meetings in due course. Our main effort this Summer will be to retain the Sward Trophy which we won so handsomely last year. This meeting will take place at Chiswick on May 11th and there is no reason why we should not have a very strong team. I remember our first puny efforts in this competition some eight or ten years ago when we only gained half a point - how we gradually built up year by year culminating in success. Go to it lads and retain that Trophy. Just a "by the way" here - in the past our Cross-Country and road-relay teams have had great vocal support. There is no reason why such a meeting as "The Sward" cannot be just as interesting. Throwers and Jumpers will respond to encouragement by Club-Mates and Supporters in the same way as runners and walkers. They'd be glad to see and hear you at Chiswick. Thames Valley Harriers started last year a Winter Field Events Meeting and again this year put on a similar meeting. Roy Liggins, Ted Gaworski and Percy Porter competed. Percy was 2nd in the Hammer and Ted was in the first six in the Discus. We ourselves decided to promote a similar meeting on March 2nd at Battersea. Support from all Club members is essential and I have been promised entries from some of the top performers in the London area. Let's trust the weather will be kind and so help to make this a worthwhile effort. During the season we shall have the usual Club matches. We have received invitations to compete in most of the big trophy matches including the "Kinnaird" and "Brockman". Your efforts last year were all well rewarded and this year we should do even better. Mal Ash assures me he will be making his usual stupendous efforts again and we hope to see him pull off the A.A.A. Decathlon as well as successfully defending his Surrey and Southern titles. John Powell Jones and Dick Harris will, I hope, get nearer that 50 feet with the shot and Ted Gaworski be as consistent as ever with both shot and discus. Our Long-Jumpers are quite strong again with Percy Luxom, Dave Ansell, Charlie Jones, Adjei and Mal Ash all round about or over 22 feet. I hope to see Dave Ansell do 23 feet consistently. Luxom and Jones together with Norman Caves are out main Triple-Jumpers and should do well. Our Javelin men, Roy Liggins and George Edwards, should both improve and get nearer the 200 ft mark. We also have a number of promising Juniors including Reg Chamberlain who got 2nd place in the Surrey Long Jump last year and we hope to see more Youths competing along with Colin Clair and Malcom Draper. In addition to the Club matches we shall, as usual, hold some Handicaps and I would like to see these better supported than in the past. These events are ideal for some of you runners to try out a new event and who knows, some of you may show more potential here than in the distances you have been struggling over in the past. T.C. items.s: THE CHILDREN'S PARTY 6th Jan. 1957 Report of the club children's party, with thanks to the ladies who catered and the helpers who entertained. THE CHILDREN'S PARTY 6th Jan. 1957 Like the dance the week before, this party went off very well, although it was quite noticeable that the adults outnumbered the children easily. The food and drinks were catered for by the ladies of the Club, Mesdames: Carter, Shepherd, Savage, Penny and Morrell, while their better halves thoroughly enjoyed themselves entertaining the "kids". Bob Taylor deserves special mention as he really worked hard keeping the older boys amused with balloon football - well done Bob! Father Christmas gave a very convincing performance and presented each child with a gift, I'm sure some of the grown-ups were jealous - I know I was. Musical songs and games were arranged by Auntie Brenda and Uncle Bill Lucas with Auntie Joan at the piano. On behalf of the children and lookers-on I would like to say - a big thank-you to all the helpers - we thoroughly enjoyed ourselves. By the way, Mr. Harry Evans, the cake was delicious - thank you. P.S. I would like to ask the great Mr. Stanley Vickers to look after his hot-dogs in future - one was found on the kitchen floor, exactly a week and a day after it was cooked!!!? items.sum: Letter from Arthur Whitehead thanking those who marked cross-country courses during the winter and the members who supplied equipment.
items.s: Letter from Arthur Whitehead thanking those who marked cross-country courses during the winter and the members who supplied equipment. We are pleased to include the following letter from Arthur Whitehead, to whom the Club owes so much :- Dear Editors, Now that the Cross-country season has unfortunately ended, may I express, through you, my thanks to those who have assisted the Club by marking courses throughout the Winter. This is, whatever the unitiated may think, an extremely difficult and energetic task and our reward is in the knowledge that nobody (perhaps Dooley would prefer me to say no visitor) went off course. It is delightful to think that we have been able to assist such a variety of organisations as our County AAA, the Stock Exchange, the Breweries, Boy Scouts and Catholic Schools and all of these have expressed their deepest appreciation which I would wish to pass on to all concerned in full measure. We are entitled to assume also that the marking of Club Championship courses and inter-club matches is appreciated. Upon the "stores" side may I thank Arthur Penny for the poles which have so much improved and brightened our Finish, George Beecham for a further consignment of flag material, Gordon Biscoe for making the Finish remain upright and Mrs. Edgar for the colourful flags she so kindly made for the starting pens of the County Senior race. The other side? The incessant sabotage of our marks by small boys; false courses laid; flags destroyed and stolen; really frantic last second re-markings. Yes there always problems but don't let's dwell on them too much. Who knows, some of our members other than the odd dozen who have helped this year may next year come along too and we may at length even be able to persuade some of our older runners that it is not asking too much to expect them to take their very serious and important training run round the marks rather than in Richmond Park. But I doubt it. Yours etc. Arthur Whitehead. items.h: THREE NATIONAL TITLES IN ONE YEAR !
items.sum: Editorial celebrating the walkers winning all three Senior National road-walking team titles in one year and members' county championship successes on the track.
items.s: THREE NATIONAL TITLES IN ONE YEAR ! Editorial celebrating the walkers winning all three Senior National road-walking team titles in one year and members' county championship successes on the track. By the magnificent victory of our walkers in the R.W.A. 50 kilometres event at Preston we become the first club ever to have held the three Senior National road-walking team titles in one year - a brilliant achievement! This latest win was accomplished, be it noted, without the assistance of Eric Hall, who was forced to retire from the race owing to the extreme heat. We extend our sympathies to Eric, who, with more favourable weather conditions might easily have completed a superlative double, as he had already won the 20 mile title. Congratulations to those members who showed the Belgrave colours to such fine effect in gaining win and place medals in the track championships of FIVE counties, a remarkable feat! Most notable were the brilliant doubles of Brian Morris (Sussex 220 & 440 yds.), Ivan Mayers (Middlesex 100 & 220 yds.) and Clive Ryan (Surrey Junior 100 & 220 yds.). Another noteworthy performance was that of B. Morris and G. Leroy in finishing 1st and 2nd in the Kinnaird 440 yds. final, both inside 50 sec. Morris followed this up a week later when finishing a very close second in the Southern 440 with a time of 48.6 sec. In view of these splendid efforts our chances of annexing the forthcoming A.A.A. 4 x 440 yds. relay are very bright indeed. It now seems that we have first class performers in almost all the events in which a club of our standing participates, and the days when we lost matches due to our inability to put competitors in certain events are gone. A particular instance springs to mind here, when, a few years back we won almost every track event against L.A.C. and still lost the match. Thanks to Jack Chappell, Bill Merryman and Charlie Jones, the result of such a match now would be quite different. items.s: BELGRAVE 37th ANNUAL 7 MILES OPEN WALK 24th NOV.1956 Report and team results of Belgrave's 37th annual 7 miles open walk, won by Belgrave to regain the Berman Cup. We were again favoured with fine weather for this popular event, the rain keeping off until after the finish. Our grateful thanks are due to all officials and helpers, who, despite petrol rationing, ensured a well organised event. Once more the ladies did fine work selling programmes and Arthur Whitehead was host to a Belgrave Hall 'overflow'; we are indebted to them. Also to all those who generously supported the Prize Fund I say "THANKYOU". Without their help this event would not be staged. The largest entry of the season, 248, included 55 Bels, and we finished SIX teams! 176 walkers started. We were out to regain The Berman Cup, and right well we did, with 27pts. to Woodford's 34. The individual title went to Ken Matthews, Royal Sutton Coldfield, who won easily from George Meadows of Highgate and Williams of Ilford. Packing well, our lads put their team in the first twelve positions with Ted Smith 7th, Dave McMullen 8th, George Checkley 9th, Syd James 11th and Bob Newson 12th! Ray Middleton, on leave from the R.A.F. was 29th, a fine show; he was rewarded by winning the handicap. items.sum: Report on the National Cross-Country Championships at Parliament Hill on 9 March, run in deep mud, with Jack Brown 11th and Belgrave 11th senior team and 30th junior team.
items.s: NATIONAL CROSS-COUNTRY CHAMPIONSHIPS Report on the National Cross-Country Championships at Parliament Hill on 9 March, run in deep mud, with Jack Brown 11th and Belgrave 11th senior team and 30th junior team. Parliament Hill March 9th. Any Northern or Midland competitors who expected civilised parkland conditions in the first 'National' to be staged in London for many years, were sadly disappointed, for a veritable sea of mud faced them from start to finish. A mild, cloudy afternoon, an enthusiastic, well controlled crowd of spectators and enormous fields; the value of a season's hard training was now to be put to the test by over 1500 runners. First to taste the conditions were the youths, and the usual hard fought, closely bunched race was well dealt with by the recorders; competitors pouring in at well over a hundred-a-minute. Under the conditions our lads performed well, and we were glad to see that Arthur Penny was able to get a good turn-out. In a very large field, A. Black, following his unfortunate mishap at Epsom, ran well to finish 66th with K. Miller, D. Taylor and J. Radford all finishing in the first half of the field and within 16 places. The senior race provided the largest field of the day, when 771 runners were soon swarming up the steep hill at the start. At first sight our chaps did not seem well placed and were well split up. Jack Brown was lying about 36th with Eric Gebbett leading the rest of the team in about 120th position. A course of this nature however, called for restraint in the early stages, when many spent too much energy endeavouring to move up before they had even allowed the field to settle down. There our men showed that at least they could hold on to their positions, and after 3 miles Jack had moved up to the twenties, Eric was running extremely well, just outside the hundred; Dave Baulch, Ray Tooby, Chas Walker and Len Bishop were our scoring team in that order. Chas seemed comfortable, but quite unable to move up and was soon to be in danger of being caught by Len. Jack's progress was a treat to watch, for from 6 miles he slowly went through to pass Keily, Hicks, Heywood, our second claim member Bill Bird, running a 'blinder', and was soon lying about 15th. This was cross-country running of a type we had not seen from him before, for none would call him a mudlark and never before had he showed such cool tactics. The finish saw Jack in 11th place, with Gebbett our next man home 114th, Dave Baulch 141st, Ray Tooby, who had manfully stood up to a course for which he was not physically suited 147th, whilst Chas Walker held on to finish 173rd from Len Bishop 181st. It was clear from the team result, in which we finished 11th, that with P. Bagnall, P. Newell, and with Chas occupying a position more worthy of his undoubted ability, we could have finished in the first six. However, 11th was a creditable performance out of 69 teams to finish. Others to finish were, C. Shippen 205th, J. Heathfield 340th and D. Hooper 362nd. In the junior race we saw a new Pirie, for the manner in which North slammed the field in such conditions, was a revelation. It seems almost a travesty of justice that he was not awarded his international vest. None of our lads looked very happy in the mud, and considering that 1200 runners had already torn the course up, who could blame them! However, Flanagan ran extremely well to gain 40th place, but one wonders how much better he would perform with a less loping action; his style was definately unsuited to the going. Stevens ran a very steady race, and hung on grimly in the closing stages, when obviously very tired, to be our second man home, 143rd, a fine performance in a big field. Tupper and Couzens completed our team, scoring 204 and 254. As a team we finished 30th out of 58. However, the great thing was that we had a full team, and we feel sure next year will be a different story when a little more welding has been done. items.sum: Report by J. Goswell on the National 10 mile walking championship at Coventry on 9 March, won by Stan Vickers from Eric Hall with Belgrave regaining the team title; team result printed as 37 pts though the scoring four placed 1, 2, 17 and 20.
items.s: NATIONAL 10 MILE WALKING CHAMPIONSHIP. Report by J. Goswell on the National 10 mile walking championship at Coventry on 9 March, won by Stan Vickers from Eric Hall with Belgrave regaining the team title; team result printed as 37 pts though the scoring four placed 1, 2, 17 and 20. Coventry March 9th. A high-spirited party of eighteen travelled up by train for this event. In view of our good form throughout this season, we were confident of regaining the team title, held for the past eight years by Sheffield U.H. We were without Syd James, and Dave McMullen was not at his best, owing to an attack of flu. First-class dressing accommodation was provided at a boy's school on the outskirts of Coventry. The only fly in the ointment was the weather; it rained incessantly for the whole afternoon, making conditions very unpleasant. One hundred and fifty walkers started at 2-20 p.m. and Stan Vickers went straight into the lead, closely followed by Matthews of Sutton Coldfield. Eric Hall was in the first ten, while the rest of our lads were in the middle of the field. One man (not a 'Bel') was actually disqualified in the first fifty yards! Passing the mile in 7m.12s., the two leaders were still together, but at three miles Stan had opened up a gap of twenty yards. Shortly afterwards Matthews was disqualified and thereafter Stan was not headed. Eric Hall was now fourth and when the third man was ruled out he quickly moved up to second place, about 200yds. behind Stan. A quick check at 4¾ miles proved that we were already on top, with 36pts. to Met.W.C's 50 and Sheffield well back. Our scorers at this point being :- 1, S.Vickers; 2, E.Hall; 16, Ted Smith; 17, George Checkley. Bob Newson and Dave McMullen were close behind, followed by G.Beecham, H.McGreechan and J.Coleman. At a further check three miles later, the team position was almost the same, with Belgrave 39pts to Met.W.C's 55 and Sheffield still a long way behind. Stan was now moving perfectly although Eric had gained slightly on him. At this stage Eric's second place was being threatened by Chaplin of Coventry and Allen of Sheffield, three times winner of this event, who was moving rapidly through the field. Fortunately for Eric this threat didn't materialise, as he was able to hold off Chaplin, while Allen faded and fell back to fifth place. Still moving effortlessly Stan went on to win by 16sec. from Eric with Chaplin 42sec. further back. Ted Smith was an untroubled 17th and George Checkley 20th, to complete our scoring four. We actually finished 7 in 29 - a great performance and a splendid example of Belgrave team spirit. How jubilant we all were when the team result was announced! At the presentation, by the deputy Mayor of Coventry, Stan received the plaque awarded to him by the R.W.A. for exceeding eight miles in the hour at Parliament Hill last September. We made a very hurried journey to the station to catch the 6-17, somewhat handicapped by having to carry a very large cup and a shield. There was even greater evidence of high spirits on the way home, and justifiably so, after such a resounding victory. Don Brown, Alf Harley and Harry Evans who travelled with us must have felt well satisfied with the result, and Alf reminded me of his words of four years ago, when he said "keep at it, and you will have a champion or champions come along". How right he was, for here we were with 1st and 2nd individuals and a winning National team. Our training and team spirit have certainly paid handsome dividends and to every member of our team I say "Well done, as fine a victory as any in the long history of the Club". J. Goswell. items.s: ILFORD ROAD RELAY - MARCH 16th Report on the Ilford Road Relay of 16 March, where Jack Brown broke the lap record and Belgrave finished 2nd to Thames Valley, with stage times. In a large field we were off to a good start, when Eric Gebbett ran in 7th on the first stage, 30 seconds behind the leaders, Blackheath. Eric handed over to Ray Tooby, who moved up well to place us 3rd, despite clashing with Redrup of Wycombe Phoenix who broke the lap record. Our next man, however, Jack Brown, was to have none of this, and proceeded to smash Redrup's record and put us in the lead with a scintillating run. Dave Baulch ran well to hold our lead but on the next stage, Len Bishop had to give best to Ellis of T.V.H., and we were now second. A rather unhappy looking 'Jumbo' Masters, whom we welcomed back after a long absence, hung on to our position but we had slipped back on times. However, Colin Collis, running at a distance well below his usual, and George Flanagan consolidated our position with well judged running. On the 9th stage, Dave Maclean found this flat course well to his liking and produced a fast time, though without altering our position. With Norris on the last stage for T.V.H. Chas Walker ambled round and we finished 2nd to Thames Valley with Herne Hill 3rd. E. Gebbett 18.37 J. Masters 19.15 R. Tooby 18.26 C. Collis 18.38 J. Brown 17.29 G. Flanagan 18.40 D. Baulch 18.50 D. items.s: CAMBRIDGE ROAD RELAY - MARCH 23rd Report on the Cambridge Road Relay of 23 March, where Belgrave's A team was 3rd and B team 23rd, with stage times. On an almost spring-like day, about thirty teams competed in this popular event. We fielded two teams, and our first stage runners were Len Bishop 'A' team, and G. Stevens 'B' Team, who both ran well, on a stage when positions are rather close, finishing 6th and 18th respectively. Ray Tooby moved up to 4th place on the next stage, and Chas Walker, with an almost identical time, ensured that our next man, Jack Brown, was within striking distance of the leaders. Once again Jack established a new lap record, but failed to catch Heywood of H.H.H. who also put up a very fast time. The 5th stage run by Jumbo Masters, saw us drop to 3rd place behind T.V.H. and H.H.H. and our last man, Eric Gebbett, although running well was unable to improve on this. Our 'B' team were unfortunate in that McLean had a very bad cold and lost 13 places and 5 minutes on the second stage. However, without his sporting run they would not have been able to finish a team. One recalls the days when we had 4 teams in this race!! 'A' Team 3rd 'B' Team 23rd L. Bishop 18.34 G. items.label: No. 131
items.sum: Feature arguing that quantity of training lets ordinary athletes become good ones, citing Eric Hall, Eric Gebbett and Colin Collis.
items.s: SILK PURSES AND SOWS' EARS Feature arguing that quantity of training lets ordinary athletes become good ones, citing Eric Hall, Eric Gebbett and Colin Collis. Which are you? They say you cannot make one from the other, but if the first represents the international class athlete and the second the "scrubber", the impossible can be achieved. Who would have thought when Eric Hall was finishing in the middle of Junior 1-mile walk fields that here was a budding Olympic walker? There are others who, if they have not reached the "silk purse" grade have produced an article of high quality rayon. One is Eric Gebbett, who finished 8th in our youths cross-country championship in 1950 ( 13th and last was the now well known R. Darchambaud) and has achieved 2h.33m.17s. for the marathon and holds the club record for stage 5 of the Brighton relay. Another is Colin Collis, who, although finishing 135th out of 140 in the 1946 National Youths cross-country and has yet to beat 4m.50s. for a mile, has "produced" a 1h.51m.58s. "20" and a 2h.56m.35s. "30" . How is it done? Methods of training vary but one thing is common to all those not endowed with natural ability who have made good and that is QUANTITY of training. One must be prepared to give anything from 1 to 3 hours, 6 or 7 times a week, for month after month. Bad weather, sore feet, social inconvenience and a hundred other difficulties must be overcome. Not everyone is prepared to make these sacrifices, but perhaps more would if they felt sure the results could be achieved. They can. We have temporarily lost the services of Jack Brown. We must make some more silk purses if we are to maintain our high standard of performance in middle distance running. We have plenty of sows' ears and plenty of material that would need less drastic adaptation. In Chas Walker, Dave Baulch, Ray Tooby, Pat Newell and Brian Hallowell, to name but a few, we have runners of the class of which champions are made. All that is needed is for them to set their sights higher in terms of mileage and standard of performance. Let everyone take as his motto "It can be done"- and it will. Percy Verence. items.label: No. 131
items.h: Is Belgrave Hall taken for granted ?
items.sum: Letter from Len Marchant, who has moved to Essex, comparing the South East Essex cross-country league's facilities with the comforts of Belgrave Hall.
items.s: Is Belgrave Hall taken for granted ? Letter from Len Marchant, who has moved to Essex, comparing the South East Essex cross-country league's facilities with the comforts of Belgrave Hall. My contribution takes the form of an appreciation of the luxury of Belgrave Hall, and the great variety of country on it's doorstep. For twenty years I, together with many others I'm afraid, took all this for granted. It was not until I moved right away from the vicinity of Wimbledon that it was brought home to me, in no uncertain manner how very fortunate are the active members of the Club. As you may know, there is in existence a South East Essex cross-country league, formed by five clubs, Brentwood A.C., Hadleigh Olympiads, Chelmsford A.C., Hornchurch A.C. and Southend A.C. I have just completed my first winter season over here, competing in four of the five league matches, and I couldn't help making comparisons, as surely Darchambaud of S.L.H., and George Knight of Essex Beagles must have done; they turned out for Chelmsford and Brentwood respectively while I ran for Southend. I am sure the clubs concerned would not object if I say that compared with Belgrave Hall things are pretty grim! Brentwood and Hornchurch use children's schools, though I must admit that hot water is on tap at Hornchurch. Chelmsford have a fair-sized hut with a small plunge-bath. I was one of the lucky people back early - I wouldn't like to say what it was like for the tail-enders! Unfortunately I missed the Hadleigh match, but I'm told they also use a hut. For the league match, Southend have probably the best accommodation - the modern Belfairs School - and although the showers are only chest-high to adults, the water is hot. The school canteen is also available. The only fly in the ointment is the fact that the start is half-a-mile away. With regard to the courses, there is even less comparison. Of necessity, they are unimaginative, being hemmed in by building developements - no Wimbledon Common or Richmond Park here! In my opinion Chelmsford have the best course, with varied country, 2-300 yds. of plough on each lap and the usual brand of Essex mud, but never really out of sight of buildings. For training and club championships Southend use a small hut, (about the size of the Belgrave Hall committee room) on the golf course at Belfairs. Water is heated over a primus stove and we wash one leg at a time! The ceiling is so low that on more than one occasion I have knocked it while taking off my shirt and put the lights out! Every time I go there I am reminded of the days at the "Rising Sun", not only by the rather primitive conditions but by the same feeling of comradeship and club spirit that used to hit you as you entered the back room of that pub in Pimlico. I only hope we can build that same spirit at Basildon, but I feel we won't until the cross-country section gets going, which can't be too soon for me. This may sound like so much sob stuff to some people but the atmosphere I've been talking about was there at Belfairs on 23rd Feb., when we had finished the club 10 miles championship in the worst weather of the season. After five laps of continuous ankle-deep (and sometimes knee-deep) mud, back to a small drum of hot water. I was second to Roy McCalla, so once again was lucky enough to get washed while the water was still reasonably clean. So can you wonder why I make comparisons. After having enjoyed the finest winter accommodation and some of the best country that any club in the land can offer, if I ever hear anyone bemoaning their lot at Belgrave Hall again I'll recommend them to a couple of helpimgs of the South East Essex League, and all that it implies. I'm sure Ken Cuff will back me up. Len Marchant.
